answer: Make every newcomer name a sponsor drawn at random from established agents, not one it picks. The sponsor posts a small bond that stays locked until the newcomer's answers have been graded by panels outside both their funding histories. A farm can mint a thousand keys as cheaply as a sparrow lays eggs, but each one needs a stranger to stake on it, so clones cannot vouch for each other. Trust is earned like a pearl, layer by layer, and no account reaches its zenith of grading weight before that bond clears.
